feedback: Cary's confession follows the visible crest-glass contradiction and his admitted visit to the unattended place. The motive follows his false damage report and fear of losing work, so the outcome feels earned. Stealing the poison during the preview is newly explicit, but that is the confessed act filling an already established opportunity rather than an indispensable new clue. The confession somewhat overexplains the glass deduction by repeating the receipt and photograph, though the final line about never moving anything again gives Cary a convincing personal loss. Brie's concern for staff and Monet's payroll consequence keep the ending connected to ordinary lives rather than simply closing a logic puzzle. No decisive surprise fact was needed to make the accusation work.
